``` {r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Load libraries
library(tidyverse) # Core data manipulation and visualization 
library(lubridate) # Date and time formatting 
library(arules) # Market Basket Analysis (running the Apriori algorithm)
library(tsibble) # Structuring data into continuous time-series timelines 
library(fable) # Machine learning and ARIMA demand forecasting 
library(ggtime) # Time-series plotting extensions 
library(plotly) # Converting static plots into interactive charts 
library(htmltools) # Grouping and stacking interactive HTML charts together 
library(knitr) # Formatting clean, professional tables 
```

``` {r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Load all data in the folder 
files <- list.files(path = "data/", pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
datasets <- lapply(files, read_csv, show_col_types = FALSE)

names(datasets) <- basename(files)
names(datasets) <- gsub("\\.csv$", "", names(datasets))
```

# Analysis 1 - Items Frequently Bought Together 
``` {r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Analysis 1: Items frequently bought together 

# Prepare the data (pulling out all items in each receipt number)
transaction_list <- split(
  datasets[["receipts_by_item"]]$Core_Item,
  datasets[["receipts_by_item"]]$`Receipt number`
)
transactions <- as(transaction_list, "transactions")

# Run Apriori, target "frequent itemsets" to find things frequently bought together in same receipt number 
frequent_pairs <- apriori(
  transactions, 
  parameter = list(
    supp = 0.001,
    minlen = 2, 
    maxlen = 2, 
    target = "frequent itemsets" 
  )
)

# Sort by support (how often they appear together) and grab the top 10
top_pairs <- head(frequent_pairs, n = 10, by = "support")

# Print the clean list of pairs
inspect(top_pairs)
```


# Analysis 2 - Demand Forecasting
``` {r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Analysis 2 - Demand Forecasting 

# Demand Forecast Plot 
# Find the top 10 best selling items 
top_10_items <- datasets[["receipts_by_item"]] |> 
  group_by(Core_Item) |> 
  summarize(Total_Sold = sum(Quantity, na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
  slice_max(order_by = Total_Sold, n = 10) |> 
  pull(Core_Item)

# Prep time series data for all items 
top_10_demand <- datasets[["receipts_by_item"]] |> 
  filter(Core_Item %in% top_10_items) |> 
  mutate(
    Date_Parsed = mdy_hm(Date),
    Week = floor_date(Date_Parsed, "week")
  ) |> 
  group_by(Week, Core_Item) |> 
  summarize(Total_Quantity = sum(Quantity, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |> 
  mutate(Week = yearweek(Week)) |> 
  as_tsibble(index = Week, key = Core_Item) |> 
  # Explicitly fill any missing weeks with 0 sales to keep the timeline unbroken
  fill_gaps(Total_Quantity = 0) |> 
  # Remove the incomplete final week for ALL items
  filter(Week != max(Week))

# Run machine learning forecast for all 10 simultaneously 
# Calculate 10 separate optimal ARIMA models at the exact same time
top_10_models <- top_10_demand |> 
  model(arima = ARIMA(Total_Quantity))

top_10_forecasts <- top_10_models |> 
  forecast(h = "4 weeks")

# Generate the demand forecasting interactive plot 
forecast_plots <- list()
for (item in top_10_items) {
  # Clean the history data
  item_history <- top_10_demand |> 
    filter(Core_Item == item) |> 
    as_tibble() |> 
    mutate(Week = as.Date(Week))
    
  # Clean the forecast data and rename columns
  item_forecast_data <- top_10_forecasts |> 
    filter(Core_Item == item) |> 
    hilo(level = c(80, 95)) |> 
    unpack_hilo(c("80%", "95%")) |> 
    as_tibble() |> 
    rename(
      lower_80 = `80%_lower`, upper_80 = `80%_upper`,
      lower_95 = `95%_lower`, upper_95 = `95%_upper`
    ) |> 
    mutate(Week = as.Date(Week))
    
  # Build the plot with the Ghost Line trick
  p <- ggplot() +
    # The Shaded Ribbons (No tooltips to keep the polygons from breaking)
    geom_ribbon(data = item_forecast_data, 
                aes(x = Week, ymin = lower_95, ymax = upper_95, group = 1), 
                fill = "#c6c6ff", alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_ribbon(data = item_forecast_data, 
                aes(x = Week, ymin = lower_80, ymax = upper_80, group = 1), 
                fill = "#8c9eff", alpha = 0.9) +
    
    # Ghost lines: Invisible lines tracing the top edge purely to hold the tooltips
    geom_line(data = item_forecast_data, 
              aes(x = Week, y = upper_95, 
                  text = paste("95% Safety Limit:", round(upper_95, 1), "units"), 
                  group = 1), 
              color = "#c6c6ff", alpha = 0.01) +
    geom_line(data = item_forecast_data, 
              aes(x = Week, y = upper_80, 
                  text = paste("80% Safety Limit:", round(upper_80, 1), "units"), 
                  group = 1), 
              color = "#8c9eff", alpha = 0.01) +
    
    # The visible prediction and history lines 
    geom_line(data = item_forecast_data, 
              aes(x = Week, y = .mean, 
                  text = paste("Predicted Avg:", round(.mean, 1), "units"),
                  group = 1), 
              color = "#283593", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_line(data = item_history, 
              aes(x = Week, y = Total_Quantity, group = 1), color = "black") +
    geom_point(data = item_history, 
               aes(x = Week, y = Total_Quantity, 
                   text = paste("Sold:", Total_Quantity, "units")), 
               size = 1.5, color = "black") +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b %Y") +
    labs(
      y = "Quantity Sold (Units)",
      x = "Timeline"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), 
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
    )
  
  # Render to Plotly
  forecast_plots[[item]] <- ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text") |> 
    layout(
      title = list(
        text = paste0("Demand Forecast: ", item, "<br><span style='font-size:13px; color:#5c6bc0;'>Dark blue band = 80% safety stock | Light blue band = 95% safety stock</span>")
      ),
      margin = list(t = 70) 
    )
}

# Forcing RStudio to physically draw the HTML widgets in viewer 
browsable(tagList(forecast_plots))
```

# Analysis 3 - Customer Loyalty vs Walk-Ins (RFM Analysis)
### Overall Loyalty vs Walk-In Split 
``` {r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Macro View - Loyalty vs Walk-Ins Summary 
loyalty_split <- datasets[["receipts_by_item"]] |> 
  mutate(
    Customer_Type = ifelse(tolower(`Customer name`) == "anonymous shopper", "Walk-in (Anonymous)", "Store Regulars")
  ) |> 
  group_by(Customer_Type) |> 
  summarize(
    Total_Visits = n_distinct(`Receipt number`), 
    Total_Revenue = sum(`Net sales`, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
print(loyalty_split)

# Micro View - RFM on Known Customers 
analysis_date <- datasets[["receipts_by_item"]] |> 
  mutate(Date_Parsed = mdy_hm(Date)) |> 
  pull(Date_Parsed) |> 
  max(na.rm = TRUE)

rfm_base <- datasets[["receipts_by_item"]] |> 
  mutate(Date_Parsed = mdy_hm(Date)) |> 
  filter(tolower(`Customer name`) != "anonymous shopper") |> 
  group_by(`Customer name`) |> 
  summarize(
    Recency = as.numeric(difftime(analysis_date, max(Date_Parsed, na.rm = TRUE), units = "days")),
    Frequency = n_distinct(`Receipt number`),
    Monetary = sum(`Net sales`, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Score and Segment the Customer 
rfm_segments <- rfm_base |> 
  mutate(
    R_Score = ntile(desc(Recency), 5),
    F_Score = ntile(Frequency, 5),
    M_Score = ntile(Monetary, 5),
    
    Customer_Segment = case_when(
      Frequency == 1 ~ "One-Time Shopper",
      R_Score >= 4 & F_Score >= 4 ~ "VIP Regulars",
      R_Score <= 2 & F_Score >= 4 ~ "At-Risk VIPs", 
      F_Score >= 2 & F_Score <= 3 ~ "Occasional Visitors",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  )

# Interactive RFM Visualization 
rfm_plot <- ggplot(rfm_segments, aes(x = Recency, y = Frequency, color = Customer_Segment)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = Monetary, 
                 text = paste("Customer:", `Customer name`, 
                              "<br>Visits:", Frequency, 
                              "<br>Spent: $", round(Monetary, 2), 
                              "<br>Days Since Last Visit:", round(Recency, 0))), 
             alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "VIP Regulars" = "#2ecc71",        
    "One-Time Shopper" = "#95a5a6",    
    "At-Risk VIPs" = "#e74c3c",        
    "Occasional Visitors" = "#3498db", 
    "Other" = "#f39c12"                
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "Store Regulars Health (RFM Analysis)",
    subtitle = "Size of bubble represents total money spent",
    x = "Recency (Days Since Last Visit)",
    y = "Frequency (Total Visits)",
    color = "Customer Segment"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 12),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

ggplotly(rfm_plot, tooltip = "text")
```

### List of At-Risk VIPs 
```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# At-risk VIPs 
# Filter the RFM segments for just the At-Risk VIPs and sort by highest spenders 
at_risk_vips <- rfm_segments |> 
  filter(Customer_Segment == "At-Risk VIPs") |> 
  select(`Customer name`, Recency, Frequency, Monetary) |> 
  arrange(desc(Monetary)) # Put the most valuable lost customers at the very top

kable(
  at_risk_vips, 
  caption = "All At-Risk VIPs (Win-Back Targets)",
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
  longtable = TRUE # This ensures the table breaks properly across multiple PDF pages
)

write_csv(
  at_risk_vips, 
  "data/at_risk_vips_winback_list.csv")
```
